title: STUDY TOPIC JESUS AND THE SPIRIT. Part 4
devotional:
Jesus’ relationship with the Holy Spirit helps us understand who we are.

As a perfect man, living in dependence on the Holy Spirit and in the power of the Holy Spirit, Jesus redefines what it means to be human. If Jesus was a perfect human, then we need to conclude that authentic, real, God-intended humanity is an expression of a Spirit-filled life. Or you could put it another way by saying, that nobody can be who they are really meant to be, without the continual work of the Spirit in their lives.

Living life in the Spirit gives us an opportunity to be ourselves, to embrace and enjoy our humanity as God intended.

We need to develop a theological and biblical anthropology, (anthropology being the study of what makes us human.) I believe, that only when we come to the realisation that we have been made by God and made for God, will we be able to understand our humanness. Our lives and body's have been bespokely designed to accommodate the person and work of the Spirit. Maybe seeing our humanity as something that needs to be an expression of a Spirit-filled life, would/could/should change our understanding of the fruit and gifts of the Spirit.

The fruit of the Spirit is far more than replacements for the works of the flesh. They are expressions of God’s high intentions for man before sin.

Joy is LOVE rejoicing,

Peace is LOVE at rest,

Patience is LOVE waiting,

Kindness is LOVE interacting,

Goodness is LOVE initiating,

Faithfulness is LOVE keeping it’s word,

Gentleness is LOVE empathising,

Self-Control is LOVE resisting temptation.

The gifts of the Spirit are far more than a demonstration of God’s power, they are expressions of his tender heart of love toward mankind, they are gifts that are given by God to his children so they can enter into life enhancing relationships. See 1 Corinthians 12:7, 14:4,5,12,26.

A proper use of the gifts of the Spirit should increase our ability to give and receive love. In 1Corinthians 12 and 14, Paul gives us a lot of teaching about the

gifts of the Spirit. It is important that we see chapters 12,13 and 14 as dealing with one subject, the use of the gifts in the context of the body of Christ.

Chapter 13, Paul’s famous passage on love describes God’s intended effect of spiritual gifts. (Maybe that is one of the reasons why the gifts of the Spirit have been a theological contentious issue. Their misuse or their not being used at all, has diminished love within the church and prevented spiritual enriching relationships.)

Many people often ask the question, ‘What is my spiritual gift?’

This is not a bad question to ask, however I think a better way to get the answer is to ask. ‘God how do you want to empower and equip me so that my life would be a continual source of encouragement and spiritual support to others?’

I think you could honestly say that the work of Spirit in us, makes us more human because we are becoming more like Jesus.

Living a Spirit dependant life is one of the ways, maybe the most essential way, we show love and faithfulness to Jesus.

If we were to think of a Spirit-filled life as a means of identifying our love for God and our commitment to him I think we would have a very different approach to life and to what is means to be faithful to God.

I hope our understanding of who the Spirit is will be transformed, and our relationship with the Holy Spirit revolutionised, so we will be able to embrace and enjoy our humanity.
prayer: Father thank you for the truth that authentic humanity needs to be Spirit- filled humanity.
